children: Employment in Canada declined by 41,700 in August 2026, missing expectations for a 15,000 increase and following a 75,100 gain in July.

Employment fell in business, building and other support services (-2.8%), public administration (-0.7%), natural resources (-2.3%), and utilities (-3.5%), while manufacturing employment increased 1.2%.
By province, employment declined in Quebec (-0.4%) and edged down in Ontario (-0.2%), while it increased in New Brunswick (0.6%) and was little changed elsewhere.
By age group, employment fell among youth aged 15 to 24 (-0.7%) and edged down among core-age workers aged 25 to 54 (-0.1%).
Public-sector employment fell 0.4%, marking a third consecutive monthly decline, while private-sector employment was little changed.
The employment rate decreased by 0.1 percentage point to 60.8%.
Year-on-year, employment increased by 217,000 in August.

title: Canada Employment Unexpectedly Declines
